consensus_summary: Consensus identifies righteousness primarily as right standing before God (justification, frequently via Christ's imputed righteousness received by faith) together with conformity to God's moral character and standard, functioning as both legal/relational status and ethical quality, often symbolized by a clean/white garment or robe; major alternatives are infused/transformative righteousness, pure ethical conduct, covenant faithfulness, social justice, and christological identification, with settled agreement on the dual core but debate over mechanism.
book_summary: Book defines righteousness as right-living: God is Right-Living by definition (His ways the measure of right); for those under His authority it is the doing of His commandments, the law kept and worn as the garment of righteous acts. Righteousness is given and reckoned by grace, not earned as debt, yet the gift never renames wrong-living right.
consensus_core_identification: right standing before God (esp. forensic/imputed justification by faith) plus moral conformity to God's standard
book_core_identification: right-living (doing of commandments / law kept as garment of righteous acts), given and reckoned by grace without renaming wrong-living right
boundary_disagreement: Consensus admits pure forensic standing as (primary) righteousness with right-living only as subsequent fruit/evidence; book requires actual commandment-keeping as constitutive of the referent itself and reclassifies any reckoning that would leave wrong-living renamed as invalid.
material_contradiction: None at the level of shared category (rightness relative to God, grace-reckoning, garment imagery); only boundary tension with pure-status views that treat living as non-constitutive.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same general referent (rightness before God involving both gift/status and conformity to His standard) and many of the same texts/imagery, so neither MATCH (cores not equivalent in emphasis or conditions) nor DIVERGENT/NOVEL (no replacement of the category, and ethical + reckoned aspects already present in consensus primary and alternatives). Book preserves the category while materially narrowing conditions and reclassifying cases: right-living becomes definitional rather than merely evidential, and renaming of wrong-living is excluded. This is classic REFINED boundary/precision disagreement.
strongest_objection: Consensus already lists ethical/infused righteousness as common and the book still cites the classic Pauline reckoning texts, so the difference could be read as mere emphasis within an already dual core rather than a material narrowing of extension.
